pubcol-w-cf9e855c567bf9fa.definition_en: breathing with difficulty after physical effort
pubcol-w-cf9e855c567bf9fa.example_simple: After running up the stairs, I was completely out of breath.
pubcol-w-cf9e855c567bf9fa.example_complex: By the time she reached the summit, she was so out of breath that she could barely speak.

pubcol-w-c00c3f57a428cd09.definition_en: no longer used to doing something you once did regularly
collocations: be out of the habit of
pubcol-w-c00c3f57a428cd09.example_simple: I used to cook every day, but now I'm out of the habit.
pubcol-w-c00c3f57a428cd09.example_complex: Having worked from home for years, he was completely out of the habit of commuting during rush hour.

pubcol-w-50db3acc1c7d3ed4.definition_en: having lost money or paid for something out of your own funds
pubcol-w-50db3acc1c7d3ed4.example_simple: The flight was cancelled and I ended up out of pocket.
pubcol-w-50db3acc1c7d3ed4.example_complex: Because the company refused to reimburse the travel costs, several employees were left significantly out of pocket.
pubcol-w-50db3acc1c7d3ed4.vi_meaning_correction: bị mất tiền, phải tự bỏ tiền túi

pubcol-w-1a7d110c9b3093c0.definition_en: no longer available for sale in a shop
pubcol-w-1a7d110c9b3093c0.example_simple: The book I wanted was out of stock at the shop.
pubcol-w-1a7d110c9b3093c0.example_complex: The popular console had been out of stock for weeks, forcing customers to pay inflated prices from resellers.

pubcol-w-8716b48f8de0ba21.ipa: /biː ˈəʊvə hed ænd ɪəz ɪn dets/
pubcol-w-8716b48f8de0ba21.definition_en: to owe a very large amount of money
synonyms: up to your neck in debt
collocations: over head and ears in debt
pubcol-w-8716b48f8de0ba21.example_simple: After gambling for years, he was over head and ears in debt.
pubcol-w-8716b48f8de0ba21.example_complex: The failing business left its owners over head and ears in debt, with creditors demanding payment they could not possibly meet.

pubcol-w-6c221eae19d388bb.definition_en: to hold the first or second position in an order of merit or standing
pubcol-w-6c221eae19d388bb.example_simple: Her team was ranked first in the competition.
pubcol-w-6c221eae19d388bb.example_complex: The university has been ranked first in the country for research output for three consecutive years.

pubcol-w-289d729ec866bf3a.definition_en: basic and not carefully made, but good enough to use
pubcol-w-289d729ec866bf3a.example_simple: The camp had rough and ready facilities, but we managed fine.
pubcol-w-289d729ec866bf3a.example_complex: It was a rough and ready arrangement, but it kept the project running until proper systems could be installed.

pubcol-w-f4da9fa4d98beec8.definition_en: to be extremely busy with things to do
collocations: rushed off my feet all day
rushed off their feet at work
pubcol-w-f4da9fa4d98beec8.example_simple: During the sale, the staff were rushed off their feet.
pubcol-w-f4da9fa4d98beec8.example_complex: In the run-up to Christmas, the delivery drivers were rushed off their feet, working double shifts to clear the backlog.

pubcol-w-a50ed0566e15cd82.definition_en: to be doing something risky that could easily lead to trouble
collocations: skating on thin ice with the boss
know you're skating on thin ice
pubcol-w-a50ed0566e15cd82.example_simple: You're skating on thin ice if you keep arriving late.
pubcol-w-a50ed0566e15cd82.example_complex: By concealing the losses from investors, the executives were skating on thin ice that would eventually give way.

pubcol-w-f0028baa571680e8.definition_en: to have far more work than you can easily deal with
pubcol-w-f0028baa571680e8.example_simple: I can't come out tonight; I'm snowed under with homework.
pubcol-w-f0028baa571680e8.example_complex: The small legal team was so snowed under with cases that they had to turn away new clients for months.

pubcol-w-308abfa9e1f238c9.definition_en: to be deceived or cheated by someone
collocations: taken for a ride by a scammer
don't be taken for a ride
pubcol-w-308abfa9e1f238c9.example_simple: He paid too much for the car and realised he'd been taken for a ride.
pubcol-w-308abfa9e1f238c9.example_complex: Elderly customers are often taken for a ride by fraudsters posing as bank officials over the phone.
pubcol-w-308abfa9e1f238c9.vi_meaning_correction: bị lừa gạt, bị lừa dối

pubcol-w-ff524b91e73e237d.definition_en: despite that; used to concede a point before making a contrary one
collocations: be that as it may, we must
be that as it may, however
be that as it may, the fact remains
pubcol-w-ff524b91e73e237d.example_simple: The plan is expensive. Be that as it may, we have no other choice.
pubcol-w-ff524b91e73e237d.example_complex: The witness may well have been mistaken about the time; be that as it may, the physical evidence still points firmly to the defendant.

pubcol-w-28bb51a8d453cd76.definition_en: to be in danger or under the risk of harm
pubcol-w-28bb51a8d453cd76.example_simple: Many animals are threatened by the loss of their habitat.
pubcol-w-28bb51a8d453cd76.example_complex: Coastal communities are increasingly threatened by rising sea levels and more frequent storms.

pubcol-w-d3d4ef553300e32f.definition_en: to be very deeply involved in or overwhelmed by something
collocations: up to my ears in work
up to your ears in debt
up to their ears in paperwork
pubcol-w-d3d4ef553300e32f.example_simple: I'm up to my ears in work this week.
pubcol-w-d3d4ef553300e32f.example_complex: With three deadlines looming, she was up to her ears in reports and had no time to answer emails.

pubcol-w-7cf7451273e5b114.definition_en: to be completely destroyed, eliminated, or exhausted
pubcol-w-7cf7451273e5b114.example_simple: The whole village was wiped out by the flood.
pubcol-w-7cf7451273e5b114.example_complex: An entire generation of the species could be wiped out if the disease continues to spread unchecked.

pubcol-w-2337fc210661daeb.definition_en: to be extremely different from each other
collocations: be worlds apart on the issue
pubcol-w-2337fc210661daeb.example_simple: The two brothers are worlds apart in personality.
pubcol-w-2337fc210661daeb.example_complex: Although they grew up in the same town, their political views were worlds apart by the time they reached university.

pubcol-w-af34a03b36a5b7da.definition_en: to be extremely happy and delighted
collocations: over the moon about the news
over the moon with the result
pubcol-w-af34a03b36a5b7da.example_simple: She was over the moon when she passed her exam.
pubcol-w-af34a03b36a5b7da.example_complex: The whole team was over the moon after clinching the championship in the final minute of the match.

pubcol-w-4decb08550f2c0e0.definition_en: to be strongly criticised for something you have done
collocations: come under fire for the decision
pubcol-w-4decb08550f2c0e0.example_simple: The company came under fire for polluting the river.
pubcol-w-4decb08550f2c0e0.example_complex: The minister came under fire from both the press and the opposition for failing to act on the warnings.

pubcol-w-6c02053d302cfad2.definition_en: to be very easy to do
pubcol-w-6c02053d302cfad2.example_simple: Once you get used to it, the software is a breeze.
pubcol-w-6c02053d302cfad2.example_complex: Having practised for months, she found the driving test a breeze and passed without a single mistake.

126eed68-19ce-439f-b45b-9259193046d2.definition_en: official warnings about unsafe conditions at a beach, such as pollution or dangerous currents

pubcol-w-442c32970a5d9e5d.example_simple: She bears a resemblance to her older sister.
pubcol-w-442c32970a5d9e5d.example_complex: The young actor bears a striking resemblance to the film star of the 1950s, which helped him land the role.

pubcol-w-f526f09b9236a88e.definition_en: to produce successful results after a period of effort
pubcol-w-f526f09b9236a88e.example_simple: Years of hard work finally bore fruit when she got the job.
pubcol-w-f526f09b9236a88e.example_complex: The government's long-term investment in education is beginning to bear fruit, with literacy rates rising steadily.

064e5e89-65e0-43fd-b163-190822ff7aff.definition_en: to support or confirm the truth of something

pubcol-w-29df712cd31c7212.definition_en: to accept that you are the person responsible for something
pubcol-w-29df712cd31c7212.example_simple: As the manager, she must bear responsibility for the team's mistakes.
pubcol-w-29df712cd31c7212.example_complex: The board finally agreed to assume responsibility for the financial collapse and offered to compensate affected investors.
